# Purpose
This script creates `Exercise_04.RData`, the file loaded when rendering `Exercise_04.qmd` and by students in Posit Cloud. Each run:

1. Downloads Chicago community areas (N=77) and suburban Cook County municipalities from the [Chicago Health Atlas](https://chicagohealthatlas.org) and [suburban Cook County Health Atlas](https://cookcountyhealthatlas.org), and combines them into a "novel" county-wide geography of community areas and municipalities of at least 4 square miles (N=202).
2. Creates city of Chicago (merged community areas) and Cook County ([tigris](https://github.com/walkerke/tigris)) boundaries for reference on the exercise's maps.
3. Downloads the exercise's health survey indicators for both jurisdictions (Cook County Health Survey and Healthy Chicago Survey) and joins them to the county-wide geography.
4. Saves the datasets, along with the functions students use to create the exercise's tables, plots and maps, to `Exercise_04.RData`. The CARTO API key used by the basemaps is also saved; it comes from the `CARTO_API_KEY` environment variable (e.g., set in `.Renviron`).

Each download is also saved as a cache file in the data directory, which is read instead when the source cannot be reached. Upload `Exercise_04.RData` to the course data pages (`https://justenvirons.org/pedagogy/GEO330/Exercise_04/data/Exercise_04.RData`) after each run.

# Settings
```{r}
#| label: settings

data_dir <- "exercises/Exercise_04/data"

# datasets and functions loaded by Exercise_04.qmd
exercise_file <- file.path(data_dir, "Exercise_04.RData")

# health atlas geographies (TopoJSON)
url_community_areas <- "https://metopio.blob.core.windows.net/lalage/atlas/3/shapes/communityareas.topo.json"
url_places_scc <- "https://metopio.blob.core.windows.net/lalage/atlas/6/shapes/SCC-place.topo.json"

# suburban Cook County municipalities smaller than this (square miles) are left out
min_place_sqmi <- 4

# health atlas indicator data by survey period and topic key: suburban Cook County
# municipalities ("place" layer) and Chicago community areas ("neighborhood" layer)
atlas_urls <- c(
  scc = "https://cookcountyhealthatlas.org/api/v1/data/?format=json&layer=place&period=%s&population=&topic=%s",
  chicago = "https://chicagohealthatlas.org/api/v1/data/?format=json&layer=neighborhood&period=%s&population=&topic=%s")

# health survey indicators: column name, display name, and suburban Cook County
# (CCHS) and Chicago (HCS) topic keys and survey periods
health_indicators <- tribble(
  ~column,      ~name,                                  ~scc_key,  ~scc_period, ~chicago_key, ~chicago_period,
  "obesity",    "Adult obesity rate",                   "JG8YZKL", "2026",      "HCSOBP",     "2023-2024",
  "safety",     "Neighborhood safety rate",             "JG8SRFE", "2026",      "HCSNSP",     "2023-2024",
  "sidewalk",   "Neighborhood sidewalk quality rate",   "JG8IQGF", "2026",      "HCSNSQP",    "2023-2024",
  "ambulatory", "Ambulatory difficulty rate",           "AMBDHSR", "2026",      "HCSIDQZ",    "2022-2024",
  "transit",    "Ease of walking to transit stop rate", "JG8OWII", "2026",      "HCSWTSP",    "2023-2024",
  "health",     "Overall health status rate",           "JG8OLNB", "2026",      "HCSOHSP",    "2023-2024",
  "inactivity", "Physical inactivity rate",             "JG8MIQE", "2026",      "HCSPAP",     "2023-2024")
```

# Functions for data development
```{r}
#| label: data development functions

# download a file to its cache path; if the download fails, the existing cache
# file (from an earlier run) is used instead. The download goes to a temporary
# file first so a failed download does not overwrite the cache.
download_cached <- function(url, cache) {
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = paste0(".", tools::file_ext(cache)))
  ok <- tryCatch({
    download.file(url, tmp, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
    file.copy(tmp, cache, overwrite = TRUE)
  }, error = function(e) FALSE, warning = function(w) FALSE)
  if (!ok) {
    if (!file.exists(cache)) stop("Download failed and no cache file found: ", cache)
    message("Download failed; using cache file ", cache)
  }
  cache
}

# health atlas TopoJSON geographies (no CRS stored), in Illinois State Plane East
# (epsg:3435) for spatial analysis
read_atlas_topojson <- function(url, cache) {
  st_read(download_cached(url, cache), quiet = TRUE) %>%
    st_as_sf() %>%
    st_set_crs(4326) %>%
    st_transform(3435)
}

# reader passed to fx_download_indicators() below that caches each indicator
# download as health_atlas_<atlas>_<topic key>_cache.json
read_atlas_cached <- function(url) {
  atlas <- if (str_detect(url, "cookcounty")) "scc" else "chicago"
  key <- str_extract(url, "(?<=topic=)[A-Za-z0-9]+")
  fromJSON(download_cached(url, file.path(data_dir, paste0("health_atlas_", atlas, "_", key, "_cache.json"))))
}
```

# Functions for Exercise #4
The functions below are shown, in the same order, in `Exercise_04.qmd`.

```{r}
#| label: step 2 county-wide geography functions

# function for combining Chicago community areas and suburban Cook County
# municipalities of at least min_sqmi square miles into a single county-wide
# ("novel") geography; community area geoids drop the Chicago place prefix
# ("1714000-") so they match the indicator data
fx_create_novel_geo <- function(community_areas, places_cook_county, min_sqmi = 4) {
  community_areas <- community_areas %>%
    transmute(geoid = str_replace(id, "^1714000-", ""),
              name,
              location = "Chicago, IL",
              type = "community area")

  places_cook_county <- places_cook_county %>%
    mutate(sqmi = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) * 0.0000003861) %>%
    filter(sqmi >= min_sqmi) %>%
    transmute(geoid = id,
              name,
              location = "suburban Cook County",
              type = "municipality")

  bind_rows(places_cook_county, community_areas) %>%
    st_make_valid()
}

# function for summarizing the county-wide geography by type: number of areas
# and total, smallest and largest areas (square miles)
fx_table_novel_geo <- function(novel_geo_cook) {
  novel_geo_cook %>%
    mutate(sqmi = as.numeric(st_area(st_transform(geometry, 3435))) * 0.0000003861) %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    group_by(location, type) %>%
    summarise(areas = n(),
              sqmi_total = sum(sqmi),
              sqmi_min = min(sqmi),
              sqmi_max = max(sqmi),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    datatable(class = 'cell-border stripe',
              selection = "none",
              rownames = FALSE,
              colnames = c("Location", "Type", "Areas", "Total Square Miles",
                           "Smallest (Square Miles)", "Largest (Square Miles)"),
              options = list(searching = FALSE, lengthChange = FALSE, paging = FALSE)) %>%
    formatRound(c("sqmi_total", "sqmi_min", "sqmi_max"), digits = 1)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: step 2 indicator download functions

# function for downloading one health survey indicator from one atlas ("scc" for
# suburban Cook County municipalities or "chicago" for Chicago community areas);
# key is the atlas topic key, period the survey period and column the indicator's
# (one word) column name. Chicago results also include other cities, so only
# community areas are kept, and their geoids drop the Chicago place prefix.
fx_read_atlas_indicator <- function(atlas, key, period, column, read = jsonlite::fromJSON) {
  results <- read(sprintf(atlas_urls[[atlas]], period, key))$results %>%
    as.data.frame()
  if (atlas == "chicago") results <- filter(results, str_starts(g, "1714000-"))

  results %>%
    transmute(geoid = str_replace(g, "^1714000-", ""),
              atlas = !!atlas,
              topic = !!column,
              estimate = as.numeric(v),
              se = if ("se" %in% names(results)) as.numeric(se) else NA_real_)
}

# function for downloading every indicator in the indicators table (columns
# column, scc_key, scc_period, chicago_key and chicago_period) from both atlases
# and combining them into one long table (one row per area and indicator)
fx_download_indicators <- function(indicators, read = jsonlite::fromJSON) {
  bind_rows(
    pmap(list(indicators$scc_key, indicators$scc_period, indicators$column),
         function(key, period, column) fx_read_atlas_indicator("scc", key, period, column, read)),
    pmap(list(indicators$chicago_key, indicators$chicago_period, indicators$column),
         function(key, period, column) fx_read_atlas_indicator("chicago", key, period, column, read)))
}

# function for formatting the indicators table, with links to each indicator's
# page on the two atlases
fx_table_health_indicators <- function(indicators) {
  indicators %>%
    mutate(scc_key = sprintf('<a href="https://cookcountyhealthatlas.org/indicators/%s" target="_blank">%s</a>', scc_key, scc_key),
           chicago_key = sprintf('<a href="https://chicagohealthatlas.org/indicators/%s" target="_blank">%s</a>', chicago_key, chicago_key)) %>%
    datatable(class = 'cell-border stripe',
              selection = "none",
              rownames = FALSE,
              escape = FALSE,
              colnames = c("Column", "Indicator", "SCC Key", "SCC Period", "Chicago Key", "Chicago Period"),
              options = list(searching = FALSE, lengthChange = FALSE, paging = FALSE))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: step 3 indicator join and table functions

# function for joining the downloaded indicators (one column per indicator, plus
# its standard error, se_<column>) to the county-wide geography; areas without
# indicator data are left out
fx_join_indicators <- function(indicators_all, novel_geo_cook) {
  indicators_wide <- indicators_all %>%
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(geoid, atlas),
                names_from = topic,
                values_from = c(estimate, se)) %>%
    rename_with(~ str_remove(.x, "^estimate_"))

  novel_geo_cook %>%
    inner_join(indicators_wide, by = "geoid") %>%
    st_as_sf()
}

# function for formatting the joined indicators as an interactive table that can
# be sorted (click a column name) and filtered (boxes under the column names)
fx_table_indicators <- function(indicators_geo, indicators = health_indicators) {
  indicators <- filter(indicators, column %in% names(indicators_geo))
  indicators_geo %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    select(name, type, all_of(indicators$column)) %>%
    arrange(type, name) %>%
    datatable(class = 'cell-border stripe',
              selection = "none",
              rownames = FALSE,
              filter = "top",
              colnames = c("Name", "Type", indicators$name),
              options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)) %>%
    formatRound(indicators$column, digits = 1)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: step 3 indicator mapping functions

# function for creating the base map shared by the exercise's interactive maps:
# CARTO basemap and reset and full screen buttons
fx_basemap <- function(map_data, carto_api_key = CARTO_API_KEY) {
  leaflet(data = st_transform(map_data, crs = 4326)) %>%
    addTiles(urlTemplate = paste0(
      "https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/rastertiles/light_all/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?key=",
      carto_api_key
    )) %>%
    addResetMapButton() %>%
    addFullscreenControl()
}

# function for creating a quintile color palette; when repeated values make some
# quintile breaks identical, the remaining distinct breaks are used instead.
# Areas without data are shown in light grey.
fx_quintile_pal <- function(values, palette = "YlGnBu") {
  breaks <- unique(quantile(values, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2), na.rm = TRUE))
  if (length(breaks) < 2) breaks <- c(breaks, breaks + 1)
  colorBin(palette = palette, domain = values, bins = breaks, na.color = "#e0e0e0")
}

# function for formatting legend values (quintile ranges) to one decimal place
fx_legend_format <- function(type, cuts, p) {
  values <- formatC(cuts, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ",")
  paste0(values[-length(values)], " &ndash; ", values[-1])
}

# function for creating hover (and click) labels with each area's name, geoid,
# type and location, and its value for every indicator ("no data" when missing)
fx_indicator_labels <- function(map_data, indicators = health_indicators) {
  values <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(indicators)), function(i) {
    x <- map_data[[indicators$column[i]]]
    sprintf("<i>%s:</i> %s<br/>",
            indicators$name[i],
            ifelse(is.na(x), "no data", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1)))
  })
  values <- matrix(values, nrow = nrow(map_data))
  paste0("<strong>", map_data$name, "</strong><br/>",
         "<i>geoid:</i> ", map_data$geoid, "<br/>",
         "<i>type:</i> ", map_data$type, "<br/>",
         "<i>location:</i> ", map_data$location, "<hr style='margin: 3px 0;'/>",
         apply(values, 1, paste, collapse = ""))
}

# function for adding the city of Chicago (dashed black line) and Cook County
# (dark red line) boundaries; they are drawn above the other layers in their own
# pane and do not respond to the mouse, so the hover labels beneath them work
fx_add_boundaries <- function(map, chicago_boundary, cook_county_boundary) {
  map %>%
    addMapPane("boundaries", zIndex = 450) %>%
    addPolygons(
      data = st_transform(cook_county_boundary, crs = 4326),
      fill = FALSE,
      color = "#7a0019",
      weight = 3,
      opacity = 0.9,
      options = pathOptions(pane = "boundaries", interactive = FALSE)) %>%
    addPolygons(
      data = st_transform(chicago_boundary, crs = 4326),
      fill = FALSE,
      color = "#000000",
      weight = 2.5,
      opacity = 0.9,
      dashArray = "6 4",
      options = pathOptions(pane = "boundaries", interactive = FALSE))
}

# function for adding a dropdown list (top right) that shows one map layer (and
# its legend) at a time; groups are the layers' group names, in dropdown order,
# and each layer's legend carries the class "indicator-legend-<position in
# groups, from 0>". The layer at position selected (from 0) is shown first.
fx_add_layer_dropdown <- function(map, groups, selected = 0) {
  map %>%
    htmlwidgets::onRender("
      function(el, x, data) {
        var map = this;
        var groups = [].concat(data.groups);
        // show the selected layer and legend and hide the others
        function show(i) {
          groups.forEach(function(g, j) {
            var layer = map.layerManager.getLayerGroup(g, false);
            if (layer) { if (j === i) { map.addLayer(layer); } else { map.removeLayer(layer); } }
          });
          el.querySelectorAll('.indicator-legend').forEach(function(d) {
            d.style.display = d.classList.contains('indicator-legend-' + i) ? '' : 'none';
          });
        }
        var control = L.control({position: 'topright'});
        control.onAdd = function() {
          var div = L.DomUtil.create('div', 'leaflet-bar');
          div.style.background = 'white';
          div.style.padding = '4px 6px';
          div.innerHTML = '<label style=\"font-weight: bold; margin-right: 4px;\">Indicator</label>';
          var select = L.DomUtil.create('select', '', div);
          groups.forEach(function(g, j) {
            var option = L.DomUtil.create('option', '', select);
            option.value = j;
            option.text = g;
          });
          select.value = data.selected;
          select.onchange = function() { show(parseInt(select.value)); };
          L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(div);
          L.DomEvent.disableScrollPropagation(div);
          return div;
        };
        control.addTo(map);
        show(data.selected);
      }", data = list(groups = groups, selected = selected))
}

# function for mapping the county-wide geography with a dropdown list of the
# indicators in indicators_geo, each grouped into quintiles (the first indicator
# is shown when the map opens; "None" shows only the geography). Community areas
# have light grey borders and municipalities dark grey borders, and the city of
# Chicago and Cook County boundaries are drawn on top. palette is any
# RColorBrewer palette name (e.g., "YlGnBu", "Purples", "Greys")
fx_map_indicators <- function(novel_geo_cook, indicators_geo, chicago_boundary, cook_county_boundary,
                              indicators = health_indicators, palette = "YlGnBu") {
  indicators <- filter(indicators, column %in% names(indicators_geo))

  # all county-wide areas, with indicator values attached
  map_data <- novel_geo_cook %>%
    left_join(indicators_geo %>%
                st_drop_geometry() %>%
                select(geoid, all_of(indicators$column)),
              by = "geoid") %>%
    st_transform(crs = 4326)

  labels <- fx_indicator_labels(map_data, indicators)
  border_pal <- colorFactor(palette = c("lightgrey", "darkgrey"),
                            levels = c("community area", "municipality"))
  groups <- c("None (geography only)", indicators$name)

  # geography only
  map <- fx_basemap(map_data) %>%
    addPolygons(
      data = map_data,
      label = lapply(labels, htmltools::HTML),
      popup = labels,
      weight = 1,
      opacity = 1,
      color = border_pal(map_data$type),
      fillColor = "white",
      fillOpacity = 0.2,
      group = groups[1]) %>%
    addLegend("bottomright",
              colors = c("lightgrey", "darkgrey", "#000000", "#7a0019"),
              labels = c("Community area (Chicago)", "Municipality (suburban Cook County)",
                         "City of Chicago boundary", "Cook County boundary"),
              title = "Boundaries",
              opacity = 1)

  # one layer (and legend) per indicator, grouped into quintiles
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(indicators))) {
    values <- map_data[[indicators$column[i]]]
    if (all(is.na(values))) next # skip indicators without any data
    pal <- fx_quintile_pal(values, palette = palette)
    map <- map %>%
      addPolygons(
        data = map_data,
        label = lapply(labels, htmltools::HTML),
        popup = labels,
        weight = 1,
        opacity = 1,
        color = border_pal(map_data$type),
        fillColor = pal(values),
        fillOpacity = 0.7,
        group = groups[i + 1]) %>%
      addLegend("bottomleft",
                pal = pal,
                values = values,
                title = paste0(indicators$name[i], "<br/>(quintiles)"),
                labFormat = fx_legend_format,
                opacity = 0.7,
                className = paste0("info legend indicator-legend indicator-legend-", i))
  }

  map %>%
    fx_add_boundaries(chicago_boundary, cook_county_boundary) %>%
    fx_add_layer_dropdown(groups, selected = if (length(groups) > 1) 1 else 0)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: step 4 correlation functions

# function for calculating Pearson's bivariate correlations between every pair of
# indicators; areas missing any indicator are left out
fx_correlations <- function(indicators_geo, indicators = health_indicators) {
  indicators_geo %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    select(any_of(indicators$column)) %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    cor(method = "pearson")
}

# function for plotting a correlation matrix, with indicators ordered so that
# closely related indicators are next to each other; method is "number"
# (correlation coefficients) or "circle" (graduated circles)
fx_plot_correlations <- function(indicator_correlations, method = "number") {
  corrplot(indicator_correlations,
           method = method,
           col = c("black", "white"),
           order = "hclust",
           bg = "lightgrey",
           tl.col = "grey")
}

# function for formatting a correlation matrix as an interactive table
fx_table_correlations <- function(indicator_correlations) {
  indicator_correlations %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("indicator") %>%
    datatable(class = 'cell-border stripe',
              selection = "none",
              rownames = FALSE,
              colnames = c("Indicator" = "indicator"),
              options = list(searching = FALSE, lengthChange = FALSE, paging = FALSE)) %>%
    formatRound(rownames(indicator_correlations), digits = 2)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: step 5 bivariate mapping function

# function for mapping two indicators together (bivariate map) in three
# categories (terciles) each, with a legend; x and y are indicator columns and
# xlab and ylab label the legend. Areas without data are shown in light grey.
# palette is a biscale palette: "Bluegill", "BlueGold", "BlueOr", "BlueYl",
# "Brown"/"Brown2", "DkBlue"/"DkBlue2", "DkCyan"/"DkCyan2",
# "DkViolet"/"DkViolet2", "GrPink"/"GrPink2", "PinkGrn", "PurpleGrn" or "PurpleOr"
fx_map_bivariate <- function(indicators_geo, x, y, xlab = x, ylab = y, palette = "BlueGold",
                             chicago_boundary = NULL) {
  map_data <- indicators_geo %>%
    drop_na(all_of(c(x, y))) %>%
    bi_class(x = !!sym(x), y = !!sym(y), style = "quantile", dim = 3)

  map <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = indicators_geo, fill = "grey90", color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
    geom_sf(data = map_data,
            mapping = aes(fill = bi_class),
            color = "white",
            linewidth = 0.1,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
    bi_scale_fill(pal = palette, dim = 3) +
    bi_theme()

  # optional city of Chicago boundary (dashed black line)
  if (!is.null(chicago_boundary)) {
    map <- map + geom_sf(data = chicago_boundary, fill = NA, color = "black",
                         linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dashed")
  }

  legend <- bi_legend(pal = palette,
                      dim = 3,
                      xlab = paste("Higher", xlab),
                      ylab = paste("Higher", ylab),
                      size = 8)

  ggdraw() +
    draw_plot(map, 0, 0, 1, 1) +
    draw_plot(legend, 0.05, 0.05, 0.3, 0.3)
}
```

# Geographic data
## Novel county-wide geography
Chicago community areas (N=77) and suburban Cook County municipalities of at least `min_place_sqmi` square miles (N=125) are combined into a single county-wide geography (N=202).

```{r}
#| label: novel county-wide geography

community_areas <- read_atlas_topojson(url_community_areas,
                                       file.path(data_dir, "community_areas_cache.topo.json"))
places_cook_county <- read_atlas_topojson(url_places_scc,
                                          file.path(data_dir, "places_scc_cache.topo.json"))

novel_geo_cook <- fx_create_novel_geo(community_areas, places_cook_county, min_sqmi = min_place_sqmi)

# check: number of areas by type (expect 77 community areas and 125 municipalities)
count(st_drop_geometry(novel_geo_cook), type)

rm(community_areas, places_cook_county)
```

## City of Chicago and Cook County boundaries
The city of Chicago boundary merges all community areas. The Cook County boundary comes from the US Census Bureau's cartographic boundary file (via tigris), which is cached by tigris.

```{r}
#| label: city and county boundaries

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

chicago_boundary <- novel_geo_cook %>%
  filter(type == "community area") %>%
  st_union() %>%
  st_sf(name = "City of Chicago", geometry = .) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

cook_county_boundary <- counties(state = "IL", cb = TRUE, progress_bar = FALSE) %>%
  filter(NAME == "Cook") %>%
  select(name = NAME) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326)
```

# Health survey indicators
The indicators are downloaded with the same function students can use (`fx_download_indicators()`), except that each download is also cached in the data directory.

```{r}
#| label: health survey indicators

indicators_all <- fx_download_indicators(health_indicators, read = read_atlas_cached)

indicators_geo <- fx_join_indicators(indicators_all, novel_geo_cook)

# check: areas with indicator data by type, and missing values by indicator
count(st_drop_geometry(indicators_geo), type)
colSums(is.na(st_drop_geometry(indicators_geo)[health_indicators$column]))
```

```{r}
#| label: save exercise elements to RData file

# set CARTO_API_KEY in .Renviron; it is not stored in this script
CARTO_API_KEY <- Sys.getenv("CARTO_API_KEY")
if (CARTO_API_KEY == "") warning("CARTO_API_KEY is empty; basemaps in Exercise_04.qmd need it")

save(novel_geo_cook, chicago_boundary, cook_county_boundary,
     health_indicators, atlas_urls, indicators_all, indicators_geo, CARTO_API_KEY,
     # functions for Exercise #4
     fx_create_novel_geo, fx_table_novel_geo,
     fx_read_atlas_indicator, fx_download_indicators, fx_table_health_indicators,
```
